For lack of a better description, you can thing of Realm as being a replacement for Core Data.
This is part 1 of a two part ToDo app where the focus is on Realm PropertyWrappers and ObservedResults.

This is the 3rd and final video in a series where we look at ways in which we can get a handle on the complexities of Xcode. In this video we will focus on the code editor
We will look at ways to move around your code and organize it so that you can do a better job of maintaining it in the future.
Throughout this video, I will introduce you to some new keyboard shortcuts but I will also be using ones that I covered in previous videos so make sure you watch those ones too.  Links are below.

eVideos.video: CommandLine Tools with Swift Argument Parser
eVideos.videoDescription:
In this video we will be creating two command line tools using Swift and the Swift ArgumentParser framework from Apple.
We will build a password generator that we can access from the terminal along with a tool for encrypting and decrypting documents.

eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 9. Hard Mode, Help and Synched Statistics
eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the final of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series.In this video we will be adding the remaining two features to our app as well as a bonus feature
* First, we are going to enable the Wordle game Hard Mode feature
* Then we will add our version of the Help screen to complete the basic feature set.
* We will then change the storage location of our statisitics data so that we can share it across all of our iOS Devices
* And finally, I will fix a bug I found and improve the share sheet presentation.

This is the 8th of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series. In this video we will adding two more features to our app.
* First, we are going to give our game players the ability to share their results using an iOS Share Sheet
* And secondly, we are going to allow our users to choose a permanent light mode, dark mode or stick with the system decision to change the color mode.
eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 8. Share Sheet and Color Mod

eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the 7th of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series. In this video we will be providing better feedback to our game players..
* We will be creating what I call a Toast View.  This is more of an andrioid concept and it is a small message displayed on the screen similar to a tool tip or other similar popup notification. A Toast is displayed on top of the main content of an activity, and only remains visible for a short time period.  We will be using this to display any warnings or congratulatory messages.
* The second thing we will be doing is displaying a new game button once a game is complete so our users can start a new game.
 * and thirdly., we will be creating a statistics view so that we can store our game results in UserDefaults so that we will be able to review our progress over time
eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 7. Toast View and Statistics

eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the 6th of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series. In this video we will be adding in animations and background colors for our board tiles and keyboard.
* We will introduce a second view for our Guess letter and animate a transition by flipping the letter over and change the background color
* We will also be changing the colors of the keys after a guess has been made to match the letter matching background colors
eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 6. Card Flip and Key Colors

eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the 5th of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series.  In this video we will be adding the logic to the Wordle game where we check for letter matches.
* We will create another Playground page to avoid the overhead of working in a full project
* We will replicate key model properties from our models and dataModel 
* We will develop and test the logic of the game
* Once we are satisfied we can copy the code back directly and reuse it in our application.

This is the 4th of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series.  In this video we will create an array of 5 letter words from which to select for our secret word, and also determine a way that we can verify that the entered word is valid.
* We will create a Playground so we can filter and generate an array of words found on a public dictionary website
* We will start adding WordleDataModel functions so we can add and remove letters to our attempted word and have it update the row
* Finally, we will use the verify the word using the iPhone's dictionary
and provide animated feedback of the word is invalid.
eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 4. Five Letter Words and Verification

eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the 3rd of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series.  In this video we will begin our UI design by creating our Game Board.
In this video we will finish the UI for or game by creating our keyboard.
We will be adding more properties to our WordleDataModel to manage color changes
We will need a new to add Key and Keyboard Views and a different way to scale the keyboard to fit our varies screen sizes.

This is the 2nd of 9 videos in the Building a Wordle App clone series.  In this video we will begin our UI design by creating our Game Board.
We will be creating our Model for each guess, and a DataModel class to handle all interactions for our view
We will also be creating an extension to the Color view along with a global Constants file to make our code more readable and easier to deal with.
eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 2. Designing the Game Board

eVideos.videoDescription:
Wordle is a word game created by Josh Wardle, a Software engineer from Brookyn, who created a guessing game just for himself, his partner and his family that proved so popular with that group that he thought he might be on to something so he released it as a web app to the rest of the world in October.
It's a Once a day game which invites players to guess a five letter word.  After guessing a word, the game tells you whether any of yoru letteres are in the secret word and wheter they are in the correct place.  You have 6 tries to get it right.
After each try, you are presented with a screen showing you how you are progressing over time.
What  I decided to do was create a free 9 part video series on how you can build the application using Xcode and SwiftUI.  I have tried to replicate the application and feature set as closely as possible, but added a couple of additional features.
This is for educational purposes and should not be submitted to the app store for obvious reasons, it is not your idea, nor mine.
eVideos.video: Wordle Clone: 1. An Overview and Application Setup

eVideos.videoDescription:

eVideos.video: Light or Dark mode?  Let your users choose

So in this video, I will show you and along the way, I will give you a small introduction to Markdown and how to use it in your playground pages

In this video we are going to see if we can apply the new IOS asynchronous concurrency methods to an xcode project with a target of iOS 14.  This will require Xcode 13.2 or later as it wasn't until Xcode 13.2 that Apple backported some of these features to targets of iOS 13 or earlier.

eVideos.video: 5. Swift Concurrency 5: Parallel Concurrency with Async Let

This will introduce you to new terms such as async and await, @MainActor, and a unit of asynchronous unit of work called a Task

A Swift Package for implementing a turnkey solution for signing up and signing in to Firebase using *email/password* or **apple**.
Solution facilitates ability to request *password reset* for email/password sign in as well as *account deletion* for both.

If an error occurs, then we need to know about it so instead of printing the error to the console we want to present an alert to our users with that error information and ask them to contact us with that information.

eVideos.video: Xcode and Git Source Control - A Case Study

eVideos.video: 2. Swift Concurrency 2: VOODO and Creating the UI

In this video, I would like to share with you a multi-page Swift Playground that I created that I use to test decoding of JSON.
You will come across JSON objects all the time and I often use it to mock data or to provide sample data in my apps.

eVideos.video: 1. Swift Concurrency 1: Creating Models and APIService
eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the first of 6 videos in the Swift Concurrency - from Completion Handler to Async and Await series.   In this first video, we will focus on creating our models from the JSON and an APIService to process the response.
We will create a generic function to handle the different api endpoints and models and use a Result based completion handler with our own designed API Error.

eVideos.video: iOS 15 Button modifiers + Location Button and buttonToggleStyle
eVideos.videoDescription:
This is a comprehensive video where we will look at new iOS 15
• button styles
• border shapes
* control size
*button roles.  
In addition I will introduce you to:

• and Toggle Buttons.  
As a bonus, I am also going to throw in the new type of alert called a ConfirmationDialog.

In this video I am going to show you how you can install and work with the Firebase Emulator suite on Mac OS for use with an iOS project.  The sample project is written for SwiftUI, but the information provided will apply to projects written in UIKit as well.

This will require the use of a Hosting View Controller.

eVideos.video: Cloning and Modifying a Swift Package
eVideos.videoDescription:
In this video we are going to look at how we can modify a Swift Package.
First we will install a Swift Package using Swift Package Manager and then find that we cannot edit it to meet our needs.
We will then clone it and install it as a local package where we will be able to modify it.

This is the third of 5 videos where I show you how you can add a UIImagePickerController to your SwiftUI app so that you can both select a photo from your photos album or take a photo with your device's camera.
In this, the first of 3 videos in part 2 where we add more functionality to our app, we will be adding data persistence to  so we can save and retrieve our images on subsequent launches

eVideos.video: My Images 2: Error Alert and Permission Checking

2. Using modal sheets or full cover sheets

eVideos.video: My To Dos SwiftUI app iOS15 update 3: Swipe Actions and Bound Lists
eVideos.videoDescription:
This is the 3rd of 4 videos in this series and I am  updating an app that I created in a previous series to use iOS 15.

This is the 2nd of 4 videos in this series and I am  updating an app that I created in a previous series to use iOS 15.

eVideos.video: My To Dos SwiftUI app iOS15 upate 1:  iOS 15 APIs, FocusState, Keyboard Toolbar and Alerts

This is the 1st of 4 videos in this series and I am going to be updating an app that I created in a previous series and I will get to that shortly.

eVideos.video: Getting a Handle on SwiftUI Layouts
eVideos.videoDescription:
In this video we are going to take a look at the SwiftUI layout system and in particular, look at how the  ignoresSafe area modifier applies to different views and then try to get a handle on laying out text views to make sure that your text is displayed the way you want it.
